title: A snapshot with money in the channel
request:
`p1` sends 30, then `p2` starts the snapshot while that 30 is still in the channel

./your_program.sh snapshot
init p1 100
init p2 50
channel p1 p2
channel p2 p1
send p1 p2 30
snapshot p2
deliver p2 p1
deliver p1 p2
deliver p1 p2
result
note: The 30 is in neither balance at the instant of the snapshot: it has left `p1` and not reached `p2`. A snapshot that records only balances loses it, which is exactly why the algorithm records channels as well.

title: What the marker separates
request:
a marker delivered to `p2`, and only then a payment down the same channel

./your_program.sh snapshot
init p1 100
init p2 50
channel p1 p2
channel p2 p1
snapshot p1
deliver p1 p2
send p1 p2 25
deliver p1 p2
deliver p2 p1
result
note: The 25 was sent after the marker, so it belongs to the future of the snapshot, not to its past. Recording it would count it twice: once in the balance `p1` recorded before it left, and once in the channel.
